column1: # captions.tsv -- the prose that goes UNDER each image in out/embed.md.
# scenes.tsv's `title` is the window-chrome title and is already a serviceable
# caption, so this file is entirely optional: a scene with no entry here gets
# its title. It exists so a doc caption can be a sentence without making the
# title bar a sentence, and so captions can be edited without touching the
# six-column scene contract that both capture paths parse.
# TAB-separated: name<TAB>markdown caption (one line, inline markdown allowed).

column2: `ash.status()` — collection settings and stored activity. This demo uses an external sampler. The settings alone do not prove scheduler health.
`ash.periods()` — one call answers "what history do I actually have?" across every horizon, and names which storage tier (raw samples, 1-minute rollup, 1-hour rollup) answers each one.

`ash.chart()` — Average Active Sessions in two-minute buckets, stacked by wait event, in 24-bit colour straight out of `psql`. The lock storm is not subtle. The glyph varies per series (`█ ▓ ░ ▒ ·`) as well as the colour, so the ranking still reads correctly for colourblind viewers and in a monochrome terminal.
`ash.top('wait_event')` — lock waits dominate this incident. Inspect transaction scope and blockers. This does not rule out other capacity constraints.
`ash.top('query_id')` — statements that experienced the selected wait. These are not necessarily blockers. Optional pg_stat_statements supplies current, best-effort text.
`ash.compare()` — baseline and incident windows. Positive `avg_delta` means more sampled activity in the incident. Compare the effective bounds and source too.
`ash.summary()` — load, waits, and query attribution for one fixed window. The output does not identify the blocking transaction.
`ash.report()` — the same analysis as `jsonb`, shaped for a machine. Paste it into an LLM, or store it as an incident artifact.
